textbookText: Figure: 4.1.2 Functional aspect of Forest ecosystem The green plants of the forest ecosystem capture the solar energy and convert it into chemical energy of food and store in their body through photosynthesis. This process is called primary productivity. The primary consumer like grasshopper, rabbit, deer etc. of the forest ecosystem derive the energy by consuming plants or plants parts. These primary consumers are eaten by secondary consumers (like wolves, frog etc.) and then secondary consumers by tertiary consumers (like tiger, hawks etc.). In this chain of eating and being eaten, the green plant form first trophic level, primary consumer form second trophic level, secondary consumer form third trophic level and tertiary consumer form forth trophic level. This linear arrangement of trophic levels is called food chain along which the energy flows. At each trophic level some energy is lost as heat and respiration so available energy decreases as one moves away from the first trophic level. The flow of energy is unidirectional. Also, organisms at each trophic level die and generate waste organic material. This constitutes detritus food chain. An ecosystem contains several food chains of each of the above types which are inter-linked forming a food web.

The nutrients in atmosphere, soil, water are utilize by green plant during photosynthesis, move from organism to organism through food chain and ultimately from all trophic levels, the decomposer break down the complex organic compounds and release back to atmosphere, water and soil again in a cyclic manner. This is known as biogeochemical cycling.

The trophic level of an ecosystem refers to the position that an organism occupies in a food chain or food web. It indicates the organism’s position in the transfer of energy and nutrients within the ecosystem. All green plants and photosynthetic bacteria prepare their own food through photosynthesis. So, producers belong to first tropic level. Similarly, primary consumers, secondary consumers and tertiary consumers form second, third and fourth trophic level respectively.

4.1.6 FOOD CHAIN AND FOOD WEB In an ecosystem one can observe the transfer or flow of energy from one trophic level to other trophic level by the process of eating and being eaten. It forms a linear chain called food chain. There are basically three types of food chain in nature: 1. Grazing food chain: The food chain that starts from the green plants and ends to carnivores (top consumer) by passing though herbivores.

Figure: 4.1.3 Grazing food chain 2. Detritus food chain: The organic wastes and dead matter derived from grazing food chain are called as detritus. The food chain that starts with detritus is called detritus food chain.

Figure: 4.1.4 Detritus food chain 3. Parasitic food chain: This food chain starts either from producers or consumers. It goes from large organisms to smaller ones without killing. Parasites are present in one or more trophic level.
Figure: 4.1.5 Parasitic food chain Biology, Grade 11 | 195

In an ecosystem, there is more than one food chain because most organisms feed on more than one organism. Even one organism may be eaten by several organisms. This form network of food chain called as food web.

Figure: 4.1.6 Food web 4.1.7 ECOLOGICAL PYRAMID At each step in the food chain a considerable fraction of the potential energy is lost as heat. As a result, organisms in each trophic level pass on lesser energy to the next trophic level than they actually receive. This limits the number of steps in any food chain. Longer the food chain the lesser energy is available for final members. Because of this tapering off of available energy in the food chain a pyramid is formed is known as ecological pyramid. It represents the relationship of organisms of different trophic levels. This relationship is expressed in terms of number, biomass or energy. Ecological pyramid is defined as the graphical representation of different parameters like number, biomass or energy at different trophic level in the form of pyramid. In ecological pyramid, producer level forms the base and successive levels make up the apex. There are three types of ecological pyramid in an ecosystem:

1. Pyramid of number 2. Pyramid of biomass 3. Pyramid of energy 1. Pyramid of number It shows the relationship between producers, herbivores and carnivores at successive trophic levels in terms of their number. The graphical representation of the number of organisms at different tropic level in an ecosystem is called pyramid of number.
